bound: MqttDecoder bounds a single frame to messageMaxSize 4194304, but clientIdentifier count is not capped; default authConfig is null and NoneAuthManager accepts all clients
driver: distinct clientIdentifier count; optional subscription count per persistent channel
entry: Default MQTT TCP 1883 in official docker run without mounted config
impact: default unauthenticated external clients can accumulate process-lifetime session/channel objects. Static evidence is strong, but no OOM or sustained unavailability was measured in this run.
retention: offline persistent MqttChannel remains in process registries until the same clientIdentifier reconnects or process restarts; no TTL or max session count found
scope_notes: No HTTP, disk, DB, Redis, admin, or special config dependency.
sink: DefaultChannelRegistry.channelMap plus ConnectProtocol.close persistent-session branch that skips channelRegistry.close and topicRegistry.clear
source: MQTT CONNECT with attacker-controlled unique clientIdentifier and cleanSession=false, followed by DISCONNECT or TCP close
static_trigger_shape: Open many MQTT connections using unique client IDs, set cleanSession=false, complete CONNECT, then disconnect. Repeat with new IDs and observe channelRegistry.counts or heap in a future probe.
title: Anonymous persistent MQTT sessions retain client registry entries after disconnect
